brief.summary: Warning: the 'sterile-nu tools' named in the task (for production fractions) are not among the available tools. Only arXiv and web search tools were provided, so no production fractions or transfer functions were computed here. Those numbers must come from a dedicated Boltzmann or production code, or be taken from the literature. Lyman-alpha forest flux-power-spectrum analyses set lower limits on the thermal-relic WDM mass that rose from about 0.75 keV (2000) to 3.3 keV (Viel+2013, HIRES/MIKE). Later limits are 5.3 keV from XQ-100 plus HIRES/MIKE (Irsic+2017), 5.3 keV from SDSS DR14 (z<4.5) plus XQ-100 (Palanque-Delabrouille+2019), 3.1 keV from the Cholla suite of 1080 simulations on Boera+2019 data (Villasenor+2022, which weakly prefers about 4.5 keV), and 5.7 keV from high-z HIRES/UVES data with k_max=0.2 s/km (Irsic+2023). All are 95% CL. The main things that loosen these limits are the IGM thermal history (a sudden temperature jump weakens Irsic+2017 to 3.5 keV), peculiar-velocity smearing, patchy reionization, and the choice of k_max (restricting Irsic+2023 to k<0.1 s/km gives 4.1 keV). For non-resonant (Dodelson-Widrow) sterile neutrinos, the standard conversion from Viel+2005 (astro-ph/0501562) is m_s ≈ 4.46 keV (m_x/keV)^{4/3} (omega_dm/0.1225)^{-1/3}. This is my own estimate from memory, not checked against the paper text in this session. Under it, the 3.1-5.7 keV relic limits correspond to roughly m_s ≳ 20-46 keV. That is far above the mass at which DW sterile neutrinos are excluded by X-ray decay limits (this needs confirming; see 1512.05369 and 1702.08430). So pure DW production as all of the dark matter is excluded, and viable sterile-neutrino dark matter needs resonant production, non-standard histories, or a fraction below 1.

literature.title: Unveiling Dark Matter free-streaming at the smallest scales with high redshift Lyman-alpha forest (Irsic et al. 2023)
literature.relevance: Tightest recent Lyman-alpha WDM limit: m_x > 5.7 keV (95% CL) from HIRES/UVES at z=4.2-5.0, falling to 4.1 keV with k_max<0.1 s/km; discusses peculiar-velocity and reionization systematics.

literature.title: New Constraints on Warm Dark Matter from the Lyman-alpha Forest Power Spectrum (Villasenor et al. 2022)
literature.relevance: Independent simulation suite (1080 Cholla runs) on Boera+2019 data: m_x > 3.1 keV, with a weak likelihood peak at 4.5 keV. Shows that the free-streaming suppression saturates at k > 0.1 s/km.

literature.title: New Constraints on the free-streaming of warm dark matter from intermediate and small scale Lyman-alpha forest data (Irsic et al. 2017)
literature.relevance: XQ-100 plus HIRES/MIKE: 5.3 keV combined (1.4 keV XQ-100 alone, 4.1 keV HIRES/MIKE alone); 3.5 keV if the IGM temperature is allowed to jump suddenly.

literature.title: Hints, neutrino bounds and WDM constraints from SDSS DR14 Lyman-alpha and Planck full-survey data (Palanque-Delabrouille et al. 2019)
literature.relevance: Large-sample BOSS/eBOSS limit: m_x > 5.3 keV (SDSS z<4.5 plus XQ-100), also reports neutrino-mass bounds.

literature.title: Warm Dark Matter as a solution to the small scale crisis: new constraints from high redshift Lyman-alpha forest data (Viel et al. 2013)
literature.relevance: Reference limit m_x > 3.3 keV (2 sigma); 1, 2 and 2.5 keV disfavoured at about 9, 4 and 3 sigma.

literature.title: Constraining Warm Dark Matter candidates including sterile neutrinos and light gravitinos with WMAP and the Lyman-alpha forest (Viel et al. 2005)
literature.relevance: Origin of the commonly used mapping from thermal-relic mass to non-resonant sterile-neutrino mass.

literature.title: Lyman-alpha constraints on warm and on warm-plus-cold dark matter models (Boyarsky et al. 2009)
literature.relevance: Mixed cold-plus-warm constraints; the right framework for a sterile-neutrino fraction below 1 or for resonant production.

literature.title: General framework for cosmological dark matter bounds using N-body simulations (Rogers & Peiris 2021)
literature.relevance: Emulator-based way to apply Lyman-alpha bounds to arbitrary transfer functions, such as non-thermal sterile-neutrino spectra, without relying on the thermal-relic mapping.

literature.title: Dodelson-Widrow Production of Sterile Neutrino Dark Matter with Non-Trivial Initial Abundance
literature.relevance: States that DW production cannot meet the relic abundance and the structure-formation bounds at the same time; useful for comparing DW against Lyman-alpha and X-ray limits.

literature.title: Note on Thermalization of Non-resonantly Produced Sterile Neutrinos
literature.relevance: Analytic treatment of non-resonant production at large mixing angles, including thermalization; relevant to production-fraction calculations.

literature.title: keV sterile neutrino Dark Matter (review)
literature.relevance: Overview of non-resonant, resonant and decay production, and the combined X-ray and structure-formation status.

literature.title: Sterile neutrinos in cosmology (Abazajian 2017)
literature.relevance: Review of DW and resonant production, the 3.5 keV line and the 7 keV candidate, and the mapping to WDM bounds.

result.summary: Using the sterile-nu server (serve-sbbn), I ran a DW (non-resonant) grid of 15 masses from 1 to 50 keV times 13 mixings from 1e-13 to 1e-7 (CSV sterile_nu_grid_DW_8d35ed.csv), plus a follow-up grid at the five DW-equivalent masses (sterile_nu_grid_DW_10ad91.csv). On this server Omega_s h^2 is exactly linear in sin^2 2theta and grows roughly as m_s^1.8. Setting Omega_s h^2 = 0.12 gives the DW relic curve: sin^2 2theta = 8.7e-9 (1 keV), 1.2e-9 (3 keV), 4.8e-10 (5 keV), 2.5e-10 (7.1 keV), 1.4e-10 (10 keV), 3.9e-11 (20 keV), 3.3e-11 (22 keV), 2.0e-11 (29 keV), 1.08e-11 (41 keV), 8.8e-12 (46 keV), 7.6e-12 (50 keV) (finding f-003). Fractions f = Omega_s/Omega_dm: 0.196 at 7.1 keV with sin^2 2theta = 5e-11. At sin^2 2theta = 1e-12: 0.025 (20 keV), 0.030 (22 keV), 0.049 (29 keV), 0.092 (41 keV), 0.114 (46 keV). These are ten times larger at 1e-11, where 46 and 50 keV overclose (finding f-004). Free-streaming length: 151 kpc at 7.1 keV, 107 kpc at 10 keV, 54 kpc at 20 keV. Delta N_eff is at most about 3e-4, so BBN does not constrain DW keV dark matter: the BBN-allowed mixing is 1.5e-8 at about 50 keV, far above the relic curve. The server reports no <p/T> or momentum distribution and no per-point Lyman-alpha flag, so the <p/T> question cannot be answered with this tool. The scan scan_DW_d94a06.npz covers 1-100 keV and sin^2 2theta from 1e-14 to 1e-6 (6400 points; 3092 overclose, 968 BBN-excluded). The exclusion plot is Figure 10: /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-lyman-wdm/runs/261019_143114/exclusion_scan_DW_d94a06.png (+ .pdf) (finding f-009). The X-ray-allowed f at each mass is (X-ray limit / relic-curve mixing) and needs the X-ray limits from d-03.

result.summary:
Conversion checked against the paper text. Viel+2005 (astro-ph/0501562), Eq. 5, gives m_s(DW) = 4.43 keV (m_x/1 keV)^{4/3} (0.25*0.7^2/omega_x)^{1/3}, with the omega_x normalization at 0.1225 (tc-...-31; cited in references.bib, tc-...-41). The paper says the masses map one-to-one when the transfer functions match, which assumes a rescaled Fermi-Dirac spectrum. The survey's 4.46 keV prefactor does not appear in the paper. It equals 4.43 keV rescaled to omega_dm = 0.12, since 4.43*(0.1225/0.12)^{1/3} = 4.461 keV. I worked out the DW-equivalent masses by hand, not with a tool, at omega_dm = 0.1225 / 0.12: m_x = 3.1 keV gives 20.0/20.2 keV; 3.3 gives 21.8/21.9; 3.5 gives 23.5/23.7; 4.1 gives 29.1/29.3; 4.5 gives 32.9/33.1; 5.3 gives 40.9/41.2; 5.7 gives 45.1/45.4 keV. The survey's 20-46 keV holds to within 0.6 keV (finding f-005).

Verified limits (finding f-006):
- Viel+2013 (1306.2314, HIRES/MIKE, z>4): m_x > 3.3 keV (2 sigma).
- Irsic+2017 (1702.01764): XQ-100 alone 1.4 keV, HIRES/MIKE 4.1 keV, combined 5.3 keV (2 sigma). Allowing temperature jumps of up to 5000 K lowers the combined limit to 3.5 keV.
- Palanque-Delabrouille+2019 (1911.09073, SDSS DR14 z<4.5 plus XQ-100): 5.3 keV (95% CL).
- Villasenor+2022 (2209.14220, 1080 Cholla runs, Boera+2019 data): 3.1 keV (95% CL), likelihood peak at 4.5 keV. The suppression saturates at k > 0.1 s/km because of peculiar-velocity smearing.
- Irsic+2023 (2309.04533, HIRES/UVES z=4.2-5.0, k_max = 0.2 s/km): 5.7 keV (95% CL), or 4.1 keV with k_max < 0.1 s/km. Peculiar velocities and inhomogeneous reionization are the main small-scale systematics.

Verbatim quotes were cited only for astro-ph/0501562, 2309.04533 and 1702.01764, in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-lyman-wdm/runs/261019_143114/references.bib. The other three limits come from arXiv abstracts (get_arxiv_metadata) and have not been cited yet. No figures were extracted.

Still open (question q-05): no post-2023 limit was found. The DESI search returned only BAO papers (dead end x-01). It is also unchecked whether 2209.14220, 1911.09073 or 1306.2314 quote their own DW or non-resonant sterile-neutrino masses or an updated conversion such as a Bozek/Abazajian-type relation.

result.summary: Partly done: the X-ray limits above 26 keV and the DW-yield check (step 4) are still open. (1) The sterile-nu server does compute keV-scale DW relic densities (answers q-01). Its DW relic curve (Omega_s h^2 = 0.12) gives sin^2 2theta = 2.545e-10, 3.946e-11, 2.022e-11, 1.084e-11 and 8.81e-12 at m_s = 7.1, 20, 29, 41 and 46 keV, with radiative lifetimes of 1.6e27, 5.82e25, 1.77e25, 5.85e24 and 4.05e24 s. The tool flags 20, 29 and 41 keV as 'overcloses' even though Omega h^2 = 0.12, which looks like a rounding quirk. Results are in sterile_nu_grid_DW_e67bfc.csv in the run directory (finding f-001). (2) At those mixings the line energies are 3.55, 10, 14.5, 20.5 and 23 keV, and the whole-halo M31 fluxes are 1.75e-3, 1.71e-2, 3.88e-2, 8.31e-2 and 0.107 ph/s/cm^2. The tool's tabulated limits exclude pure DW at 7.1 keV (NuSTAR M31 Roach+2020 and XMM blank sky Dessert+2020) and at 20 keV (NuSTAR M31). It has no tabulated limit within 30% in mass at 29, 41 or 46 keV, so those masses are uncovered rather than allowed (f-002). (3) The published limits covering 10-50 keV are from NuSTAR Galactic Center observations (Perez+2017, arXiv:1609.00667), which the abstract describes as the strongest over most of that range. Only the abstract was read, so numerical sin^2 2theta limits at 29-46 keV were not extracted (f-008, q-06). (4) For the mixed-model Lyman-alpha bound, Boyarsky+2009 (arXiv:0812.0010, cite-validated in references.bib) allow any m_NRP > 5 keV when F_WDM < 0.6 (99.7% frequentist) or F_WDM < 0.35 (Bayesian 95%). Their pure-WDM bounds are m_NRP > 8 keV (99.7%) and 12.1 keV (95%) (f-007). Pure DW is excluded by the tool's X-ray limits for m_s up to about 20 keV. That rules out the conservative end of the Lyman-alpha DW-equivalent range, but exclusion at 29-46 keV still needs the NuSTAR numbers. Not done: the papers 1702.08430, 1705.01837, 1706.03118, 2007.13751, 2006.09553 and 1512.05369 were not read, so no DW-yield revision was checked. No figures were produced.

result.summary:
I could not get numerical NuSTAR sin^2 2theta limits at 20, 29, 41 or 46 keV, so there is no f_X(m_s) table and no f_X comparison with the Boyarsky+2009 bound (F_WDM < 0.35-0.6). Pure DW comes out excluded across 20-46 keV, but only by inference from the Perez+2017 text, not from numbers.

What was established:
(1) Perez+2017 (arXiv:1609.00667; full text in run_dir/1609.00667.txt, tc-...-69, -76, -78). The paper states 'Assuming the νMSM framework, our limit translates into an upper limit on the sterile neutrino mass of mχ ≲ 16 keV'. In its Fig. 8 the upper edge of the nuMSM band is the non-resonant (DW) production line. So the NuSTAR GC limit lies below the DW relic mixing for m_s above about 16 keV, across its 10-50 keV coverage. INTEGRAL covers m_s above 50 keV and is said to rule out mixing-produced sterile neutrinos as all of the dark matter. My inferred verdict is that pure DW is X-ray excluded at 20, 29, 41 and 46 keV. Caveat: the paper notes a weakening ('bump') of its limit near 40 keV, so 41 keV is the least secure point (f-012, medium confidence).
(2) Perez+2017 Eq. 5 gives the flux normalization F ≈ 2.6e-6 cm^-2 s^-1 (m/20 keV)^4 (sin^2 2theta/1e-14) for the default coreNFW profile (J_tot = 29 GeV cm^-3 kpc sr^-1, dOmega ≈ 3.8 deg^2). From this, the DW relic point at 20 keV predicts about 7e-3 ph/cm^2/s; this is my hand calculation (f-013).
(3) The sterile-nu tool returns no limit values. At 20 keV and sin^2 2theta = 3.946e-11 it reports EXCLUDED by NuSTAR M31 (Roach+2020), with an M31 flux of 0.0171 ph/s/cm^2. At 29 keV and 2.022e-11 it reports excluded_by = [] ('not excluded within 30% in mass'), with E = 14.5 keV and tau = 1.77e25 s. That 29 keV result is a coverage gap, not an allowed region. f-002 therefore cannot be backed by a quoted tool limit value; it rests on the verdict strings only (f-014).

What failed: get_paper_figures could not render Figs. 6-8 of 1609.00667, since the HTML has only Figs. 3 and 4 (dead end x-03). Roach+2020/2023 were not checked, and Perez+2017 was not added to references.bib because the budget ran out.

Still open: q-06 and q-07 (numerical limits at 29-46 keV and the f_X table), and q-04 (comparing f_X with Boyarsky+2009).

directions.rationale: The critic estimates the server is about 2.5x more efficient than the Abazajian fit at 3 keV and exactly linear rather than power 1.23 in mixing. result.summary:
Two success criteria are met (relic-mixing ratios at six masses, revised fractions f with the normalization stated) and the corrected Delta N_eff statement is recorded as an analytic estimate. The cite() step was not done. All numbers below except the fit itself are my hand arithmetic from that fit, not tool output.

(1) Literature yield (f-015). Abazajian 2005 (astro-ph/0511630, Eq. 7), read verbatim, gives m_s = 3.40 keV (sin^2 2theta/1e-8)^-0.615 (Omega_DM/0.26)^0.5 x {0.527 erfc[-1.15 (T_QCD/170 MeV)^2.15]}. The braced factor equals 1 at T_QCD = 170 MeV, and the fit is valid for 135 < T_QCD < 300 MeV. This means Omega_s scales as (sin^2 2theta)^1.23 m_s^2, whereas the server is linear in mixing and goes roughly as m_s^1.8. Paper text: astro-ph_0511630.txt in the run directory.

(2) Relic-curve correction (f-016). The literature relic mixings are 1.23e-8 (3 keV), 3.02e-9 (7.1 keV), 5.6e-10 (20 keV), 3.06e-10 (29 keV), 1.75e-10 (41 keV) and 1.45e-10 (46 keV). These are 10.2x, 12.1x, 14.4x, 15.3x, 16.1x and 16.4x the server's f-003 values, so the critic's 2.5x estimate understates the gap. The f-001 and f-003 mixings should be scaled up by about 10-16.

(3) Revised fractions (f-017). At 7.1 keV, f = 0.0064 for sin^2 2theta = 5e-11 and 0.0098 for 7e-11, consistent with the literature figure of about 1%. The server gives 0.196 at 5e-11. At sin^2 2theta = 1e-12, f = 4.2e-4 (20 keV), 8.8e-4 (29 keV), 1.75e-3 (41 keV) and 2.2e-3 (46 keV), 50-60x below f-004. At 1e-11 nothing overcloses.

(4) Delta N_eff (f-018). On the relic curve Delta N_eff ≈ 11.3 eV / m_s: 1.6e-3 at 7.1 keV, 5.6e-4 at 20 keV and 2.5e-4 at 46 keV. This confirms the critic's 1.6e-3, and f-004's 'at most 3e-4' holds only above about 40 keV. BBN and the CMB do not constrain these values. This is an analytic estimate that does not depend on the yield normalization.

Caveats: Asaka-Laine-Shaposhnikov (hep-ph/0612182, abstract only) find results that 'differ moderately' and allow DW as all of the dark matter only below 3.5 keV (6 keV at most). The updated yields in 1705.01837 and Venumadhav+2016 were not read.

Still open (q-08): the cite() call with the verbatim Eq. 7 quote into references.bib, and checking the 2017 and 2016 yields.

result.summary:
I built a side-by-side table of NRP/DW-equivalent masses under two relations (finding f-010). I did the arithmetic by hand; no tool computed it. The relations are Viel+2005 Eq. 5 (4.43 keV m_x^{4/3}, omega = 0.1225; verified in d-02) and a Bozek+2016-type relation (3.9 keV m_x^{1.294}). I took the Bozek coefficients from the direction card and could not confirm them in any paper text: the abstract search found nothing and the 2007.13751 abstract quotes no relation. Treat that column as unverified.

| m_x (keV) | Viel+2005 (keV) | Bozek-type (keV) |
|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | 20.0 | 16.9 |
| 3.3 | 21.8 | 18.3 |
| 3.5 | 23.5 | 19.7 |
| 4.1 | 29.1 | 24.2 |
| 5.3 | 40.9 | 33.8 |
| 5.7 | 45.1 | 37.1 |

Under the alternative relation the DW-equivalent range moves from 20-45 keV to 17-37 keV, lower by 3-8 keV.

Of the abstracts checked, only Boyarsky+2009 (0812.0010) quotes NRP masses itself: m_NRP > 8 keV (99.7%) and > 12.1 keV (Bayesian 95%). Inverting Viel+2005 by hand gives m_x of about 1.56 and 2.12 keV, weaker than modern limits. The Irsic+2017 (1702.01764) and Palanque-Delabrouille+2019 (1911.09073) abstracts quote only thermal-relic masses (5.3 keV; 3.5 keV for Irsic+2017 with temperature jumps), so their DW masses depend entirely on a mapping relation (finding f-011).

The post-2023 search found nothing (dead end x-02). Neither query ('one-dimensional flux power spectrum warm dark matter 2024' or 'Lyman-alpha P1D emulator thermal relic warm dark matter mass limit DESI eBOSS') returned a DESI DR1, eBOSS or emulator WDM limit, only DESI BAO papers (2404.03001, 2503.14739).

Still open: q-05 should be retried with web_search or arxiv_agent using author names; the Bozek+2016 relation needs checking against its source; and I did not check whether 2209.14220 and 1306.2314 quote their own NRP masses. No files or figures were produced.

findings.claim: Of the abstracts checked, only Boyarsky+2009 (0812.0010) quotes non-resonant (NRP) sterile-neutrino masses directly: m_NRP > 8 keV (99.7%, frequentist) and > 12.1 keV (Bayesian 95%). Inverting Viel+2005 by hand, these correspond to thermal-relic masses of about 1.56 and 2.12 keV, which are older and weaker than the 3.1-5.7 keV limits. The abstracts of Irsic+2017 (1702.01764) and Palanque-Delabrouille+2019 (1911.09073) give only thermal-relic masses (5.3 keV for both; 3.5 keV for Irsic+2017 with temperature jumps), so the DW-equivalent values for them come entirely from a mapping relation.

Perez+2017 (arXiv:1609.00667, NuSTAR Galactic Center 0-bounce photons) states in the text that, within the nuMSM, its limit gives an upper bound on the sterile-neutrino mass of m_chi below about 16 keV. The nuMSM allowed band in its Fig. 8 lies between the non-resonant (DW) production line above and the maximum-lepton-asymmetry resonant line below. So the NuSTAR GC limit lies below the whole band, including the DW line, at masses above about 16 keV and up to the edge of its 10-50 keV coverage. Above 50 keV, INTEGRAL limits rule out mixing-produced sterile neutrinos as all of the dark matter. Together these imply pure DW is X-ray excluded at m_s = 20, 29, 41 and 46 keV. This is an inference from the paper's text, not from numerical sin^2 2theta values. The paper notes the limit weakens near 13 and 40 keV ('bumps'), which is a caveat for 41 keV.

findings.claim: Perez+2017 Eq. 5 gives the GC decay-line flux as F ≈ 2.6e-6 cm^-2 s^-1 (m/20 keV)^4 (sin^2 2theta/1e-14)(dOmega/4 deg^2)(J/40 GeV cm^-3 kpc sr^-1), with dOmega_tot ≈ 3.8 deg^2 and J_tot = 29 GeV cm^-3 kpc sr^-1 for the default coreNFW profile. Applied to the DW relic mixing at 20 keV (3.9e-11), this predicts about 7e-3 ph/cm^2/s in the NuSTAR 0-bounce aperture (my hand calculation). Numerical flux and sin^2 2theta limits are shown only in Figs. 6-8, which are not machine-readable here.

The sterile-nu tool's X-ray verdicts at the DW relic mixing give only a list of excluding limits, never the limit value itself. At m_s = 20 keV, sin^2 2theta = 3.946e-11, the M31 flux is 0.0171 ph/s/cm^2 and the result is 'EXCLUDED by: NuSTAR M31 (Roach+ 2020)'. At m_s = 29 keV, sin^2 2theta = 2.022e-11 (E = 14.5 keV, tau = 1.77e25 s, M31 flux 0.0388, MW-center whole-halo flux 264 ph/s/cm^2), the result is 'Not excluded by tabulated X-ray limits (within 30% in mass)' with excluded_by = []. So f-002 cannot be backed by a numerical limit from this tool, and its 29 keV 'not excluded' is a coverage gap, not an allowed region.

Abazajian 2005 (astro-ph/0511630, Eq. 7, full numerical DW calculation with the QCD transition, nu_e mixing): m_s = 3.40 keV (sin^2 2theta/1e-8)^(-0.615) (Omega_DM/0.26)^0.5 x {0.527 erfc[-1.15 (T_QCD/170 MeV)^2.15]}. The braced factor is 1 at T_QCD = 170 MeV, and the fit is valid for 135 < T_QCD < 300 MeV. Inverted, this gives Omega_s = 0.26 (m_s/3.4 keV)^2 (sin^2 2theta/1e-8)^1.23. Compared with the server's linear scaling in mixing and roughly m^1.8 in mass, the literature yield goes as mixing^1.23 and m_s^2. The peak production temperature is T_peak ~ 130 MeV (m_s/3 keV)^(1/3).

findings.claim: Literature DW relic mixing from the Abazajian 2005 Eq. 7 (my hand calculation, Omega_DM = 0.26, T_QCD = 170 MeV): sin^2 2theta = 1.23e-8 (3 keV), 3.02e-9 (7.1 keV), 5.61e-10 (20 keV), 3.06e-10 (29 keV), 1.75e-10 (41 keV), 1.45e-10 (46 keV). The server's relic curve (f-003) lies 10.2x, 12.1x, 14.4x, 15.3x, 16.1x and 16.4x lower in mixing at these masses. So the server overproduces DW sterile neutrinos at fixed mixing by more than the critic's 2.5x estimate. The f-001 and f-003 relic mixings should be multiplied by about 10-16 to match this fit. Using Omega_DM = 0.264 (h = 0.674) raises the literature mixings by only about 1%.

findings.claim: Revised DW fractions under the Abazajian 2005 yield, f = (sin^2 2theta / sin^2 2theta_relic)^1.23 normalized to Omega_DM = 0.26 (my hand calculation): at 7.1 keV, f = 0.0064 for sin^2 2theta = 5e-11 and 0.0098 for 7e-11. This matches the literature statement of about 1% of the dark matter at the 3.5 keV-line mixing, whereas the server gives 0.196 and 0.27 (about 30x higher). At sin^2 2theta = 1e-12: f = 4.2e-4 (20 keV), 8.8e-4 (29 keV), 1.75e-3 (41 keV), 2.2e-3 (46 keV), against the server's 0.025, 0.049, 0.092 and 0.114 (50-60x too high). At 1e-11, multiply by 10^1.23 = 17: f = 7e-3 (20 keV) to 0.037 (46 keV), so nothing overcloses. Overall, f-004's fractions are overstated by 1.5-2 orders of magnitude.

Corrected Delta N_eff statement: on the relic curve the sterile number density is fixed by Omega_s h^2 / m_s, whatever yield normalization is used. My hand estimate, assuming one Weyl species and n_s/n_nu = Omega_s h^2 x 94 eV / m_s, gives Delta N_eff ≈ 11.3 eV / m_s while relativistic: 1.6e-3 at 7.1 keV, 5.6e-4 at 20 keV, 2.5e-4 at 46 keV. This matches the critic's 1.6e-3 on-curve value at 7.1 keV, so f-004's 'at most 3e-4' holds only above about 40 keV. All values are 2-3 orders of magnitude below BBN and Planck sensitivity (about 0.2-0.3), so BBN does not constrain keV DW dark matter.

issues.text: The sterile-nu server is serve-sbbn.sh. Its probes (the eV-scale SBL anomaly check, BBN Yp and D/H, N_eff) suggest it may only model thermalized light steriles, not keV Dodelson-Widrow freeze-in. Make step 1 a hard gate. If describe_sterile_nu_tools or a single predict_sterile_nu call at 7.1 keV does not return a non-resonant relic fraction, stop the grid and scan. Report that the production fractions must come from the literature, and do not interpolate a relic curve from outputs that are out of validity.

Add a robustness cross-check. Compare the tool's DW relic curve at 2-3 masses against a published analytic DW abundance, for example the Abazajian/Asaka fits in 1705.01837. Without this, f values tied only to tool calls cannot be verified. Also note that predict_sterile_nu_grid and scan_sterile_nu_parameters overlap; drop the scan if the grid already gives the plane, and save the calls.

This does not fit 13 calls. Six papers, each needing download, chunk reads and cite, plus a post-2023 search, needs about 20 or more calls. Prioritize Viel+2005 for the conversion and 2309.04533 and 1702.01764 for the limits and systematics, all with full text. Take 2209.14220, 1911.09073 and 1306.2314 from abstracts or metadata, flagged as abstract-level. Drop the optional figure step.

Several of these papers quote their own NRP sterile-neutrino-equivalent masses. Irsic+2017 and Palanque-Delabrouille+2019 are examples, and they use updated conversions that differ from the Viel+2005 4/3 power law. Report both the paper-quoted value and the formula-derived value side by side, rather than overwriting one with the other. The brief also lists k_1/2 and the suppression at k=10 h/Mpc for DW versus thermal relics, but no direction assigns them. Fold one quote on transfer-function shape differences, DW versus thermal (for example from 1705.01837 or 2007.13751), into this direction, or state that it is out of scope.

Step 1 runs X-ray line predictions with survey-estimated mixing angles before d-01 delivers the relic curve. Those results would rest on unverified inputs. Either make the step depend on d-01's output, or use one predict_sterile_nu_grid call that returns the X-ray fields rather than five separate calls. The same validity gate as d-01 applies: if the server does not cover keV decays, take the line flux from the literature.

The scope is broad for 13 calls: X-ray limits, mixed-fraction bounds, and DW yield revisions. Limit full-text reads to one X-ray limit compilation (1702.08430 or a recent NuSTAR paper) and one mixed-model Lyman-alpha paper (Baur+2017 or Boyarsky+2009). Handle 1512.05369 and 2006.09553 from abstracts only.

issues.text: The cross-check against a published DW yield requested in c-01 was not done, and the server normalization looks off. The Abazajian (2005) fit, Omega_s h^2 ~ 0.1 (sin^2 2theta/3e-9)^1.23 (m_s/3 keV)^1.8, needs about 3e-9 at 3 keV for the full relic abundance. The server gives 1.2e-9, a factor of about 2.5 more efficient. The server is also exactly linear in sin^2 2theta, where the fit has power 1.23. The literature result is that DW at the 3.5 keV-line mixing (about 7e-11) yields only about 1% of the dark matter. The server's f = 0.196 at 5e-11 is roughly 10-20x higher. The direction of the overall conclusion likely survives: a lower DW yield means larger relic mixing and stronger X-ray exclusion. The tabulated f values and relic-curve mixings should not be reported as literature-grade until this is reconciled. Note also that the arithmetic itself checks out: 1 keV gives 0.12/1.384e-5 x 1e-12 = 8.67e-9, 22 keV gives 3.32e-11, and the slope is 22^1.8 = 261.

The lifetime values in f-001 are not in its cited evidence (tc-26, tc-35); they appear only in tc-36 to tc-40. In addition, 3 of the 5 points at Omega_s h^2 = 0.12 are flagged 'overcloses', which shows the overclosure threshold is applied with a strict or rounded inequality. Points sitting exactly on the relic curve should not be labelled overclosing in any table or figure.

The verdict on pure DW at 29-46 keV (the Lyman-alpha-allowed masses under the stronger limits) still rests on NuSTAR numbers that have not been extracted (q-06). Without them, the headline 'pure DW excluded' is shown only for the conservative 20 keV end. tc-51 (a two-sterile-neutrino oscillation paper) is irrelevant evidence for f-008.

The arithmetic is correct: 4.43 x 3.1^{4/3} = 20.0 keV and 4.43 x 5.7^{4/3} = 45.1 keV. However, the visible excerpt of tc-31 shows only the title page, not Eq. 5. More importantly, only the Viel+2005 relation was used. Later relations, such as the Bozek+2016-type m_s ~ 3.9 keV (m_x/keV)^1.294 and the paper-quoted NRP masses in Irsic+2017 and Palanque-Delabrouille+2019, can shift the 20-46 keV range by several keV. c-01 asked for paper-quoted and formula-derived values side by side, and this has not been done.

The provenance of the NuSTAR/XMM and Lyman-alpha curves overlaid in Figure 10 is not documented. The tool's built-in limits have known gaps at 29-46 keV, so the figure should state which limit set is drawn and where coverage ends.

q-04 is unresolved: the X-ray-allowed f at each mass has not been combined with the Boyarsky+2009 mixed bound. Two further points are needed for a correct comparison. First, Boyarsky's m_NRP uses its own NRP mapping. Second, a DW component with f << 0.35 is trivially allowed by Lyman-alpha, so the meaningful statement is whether such a sub-dominant component is of any physical interest.

contested.reason: The arithmetic is correct: 3.9*3.1^1.294 = 16.9 and 3.9*5.7^1.294 = 37.1. However, none of the evidence excerpts contains the 3.9 keV / 1.294 relation. tc-82 is an unrelated search hit about UHE neutrino damping and two-sterile oscillations. tc-84 is an abstract that, as the finding itself admits, quotes no relation. The claimed shift of the DW range to 17-37 keV therefore rests on unverified coefficients. This relation is commonly attributed to Abazajian 2006 (astro-ph/0512631), not Bozek+2016, and should be checked against that source.

Neither quoted excerpt contains the claimed statements. tc-76 is the title and author block. tc-78 is the NFW-profile and local-density passage. The excerpts include neither 'm_chi <~ 16 keV', nor the Fig. 8 band-edge description, nor the 13/40 keV 'bump' remark, nor the INTEGRAL statement. The title supports the general thrust, but the specific claims are unevidenced. The exclusion at 29-46 keV is an inference from figures that were never read.

Eq. 5, dOmega = 3.8 deg^2 and J_tot = 29 do not appear in the quoted excerpt, which is the NFW-profile passage. The hand arithmetic is correct (2.6e-6 * 3900 * 0.95 * 0.725 = 7.0e-3). However, it uses the server relic mixing of 3.9e-11, which f-016 of this same wave says is about 14x too low. With the literature mixing of 5.6e-10, the predicted flux is about 0.1 ph/cm^2/s, so the finding is internally inconsistent with the wave's own correction.

The only content excerpt (tc-81) shows Eq. 4, the lepton-asymmetry potential, not Eq. 7, and tc-70 is a download path. The quoted Eq. 7 form matches the commonly cited Abazajian fit, and the inversion is algebraically correct, but the verbatim fit is absent from the evidence and the cite() step was skipped. The interpretation that the yield goes as mixing^1.23 is also physically misleading. At fixed mass, DW production is linear in sin^2 2theta for small mixing. The -0.615 exponent of the relic-curve fit encodes the mass dependence (g*(T_peak)) along the Omega = const curve, not a nonlinear dependence on mixing.

This depends entirely on f-015, whose Eq. 7 is absent from the evidence. The arithmetic checks out: 3.02e-9 at 7.1 keV, 5.61e-10 at 20 keV and 1.45e-10 at 46 keV, giving ratios of 12-16x to the server. It has not been tested whether the server offset reflects a flavor, Omega vs Omega h^2, or g* convention difference rather than genuine overproduction.

This applies f = (s/s_relic)^1.23 at fixed mass, which misuses a relic-curve fit. At fixed m_s the DW abundance is linear in sin^2 2theta, so f = s/s_relic. That gives f of about 0.017 at 7.1 keV for 5e-11 (not 0.0064) and 0.023 for 7e-11. At 1e-12 it gives f of about 1.8e-3 (20 keV) and 6.9e-3 (46 keV), 2.5-4x larger than claimed. The claimed match to the literature value of about 1% is therefore partly coincidental. Eq. 7 is also not in the evidence.
